_comment: THE FOUNDER'S PLAYBOOK — periodical harvest config. Add future companies by editing THIS data, not periodical_harvest.py. 2026-09-25 REWRITE of the Chronicling America / HathiTrust / Google Books query sets after the three routes were debugged (see HARVEST_README.md 'What was wrong' + raw probes in ../founders_playbook/00_universe/harvest/_probe_fixed_20260925/). Endpoint status: HathiTrust VERIFIED LIVE 200 with real records; Google Books legacy Atom feed VERIFIED LIVE 200 keyless (no snippet text); Chronicling America request shape corrected to the relocated canonical host but the whole www.loc.gov zone answers a Cloudflare bot challenge to scripted clients, so CA rows are UNANSWERED until a browser egress runs them — NEVER read a CA row as a null.

chronicling_america.working_shape: https://www.loc.gov/chroniclingamerica/search/pages/results/?andtext=<quoted-phrase>&format=json[&page=N]  (page search: documented params andtext/format/page). Directory: /search/titles/results/?terms=<q>&format=json. Bulk inventory: /bulk/?format=json.
chronicling_america.what_was_wrong: (1) the base was the retired host: every chroniclingamerica.loc.gov path now answers HTTP 308 to www.loc.gov/chroniclingamerica/<same path>, and because urllib followed it silently the sidecar recorded the OLD url next to the NEW host's bytes; (2) Accept was '*/*' for every family; (3) the query content was wrong (token 'waltons', Newport mis-stated, no hyphenated brand, no Arkansas anchors).
chronicling_america.residual_block: www.loc.gov returns HTTP 403 + 'Just a moment...' with Cf-Mitigated: challenge on EVERY path tested, including /robots.txt, from a declared-tool UA, from a Chrome UA with a full Chrome header set, and from a second independent egress — while labs.loc.gov (200), data.labs.loc.gov (200), tile.loc.gov (301) and web.archive.org (200) answer normally from the same machine. That is bot management on that zone, not this IP and not this query. PROVEN, NOT INFERRED, 2026-09-25T13:48Z: https://www.loc.gov/robots.txt — a request that carries no query, no company name and no parameter of ours — answers the identical 403 / Cf-Mitigated: challenge / 'Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue' (5,457 B, CF-RAY a40a7d531c454700-DEL, Server: cloudflare). robots.txt cannot be mis-shaped by our query grammar, so the block is THEIR POLICY, not OUR REQUEST. Needs a browser session or LOC-granted access; the canary tasks below exist so the next scheduled run can prove or disprove it from GitHub's egress with 2 requests instead of 12.
chronicling_america.unverified: date1/date2/dateFilterType/state/sort/withText are LEGACY params, absent from the published docs and unverifiable while the zone challenges. A 0 from them indicts the parameter, not the corpus.

hathitrust.working_shape: https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/ls?field1=ocr;q1=<quoted phrase + place terms>;a=srchls;lmt=ft[;facet=bothPublishDateRange:%221960-1969%22]  — SEMICOLON-separated SFX grammar, action a=srchls, lmt=ft for full view. Date facet FIELD is bothPublishDateRange, value a decade or a year, copied from the site's own hrefs.
hathitrust.what_was_wrong: (1) the code called the legacy /cgi/ls/one alias with &-separated searchtype/target/ft, which answers 302 to the shape above; (2) status 0 was a CLIENT-SIDE TLS trust failure ('certificate has expired' from Python's own verifier while the environment clock is at 2026-09-25) recorded as a bare 0 with no reason — not a bot-block and not an empty catalogue; run with --insecure-hosts babel.hathitrust.org, which is how the counts below were obtained; (3) format=json is accepted and IGNORED (HTML comes back), so any '0 results' reading must come from the record blocks, not from a JSON key.
hathitrust.verified_counts: 2026-09-25, HTTP 200 each: '"Wal-Mart" Bentonville' -> All Items 11,850 / Full View 2,638, 100 record blocks; + facet bothPublishDateRange:"1960-1969" -> 45 / 4; '"Walton's" "five-and-dime"' -> 1,529 / 59; CONTROL '"five and dime" variety store' + 1950-1959 -> 2,284 / 187. THE WINDOW IS INTERMITTENT, NOT OPEN: the SAME URL bytes ("Wal-Mart" Bentonville, unbounded and faceted) re-run at 13:44-13:52Z returned 403 Cf-Mitigated: challenge five times in a row (declared-tool UA, Chrome UA + full Chrome header set, spaced retries) while catalog.hathitrust.org/api/volumes/brief/htid/uiug.30112005545535.json answered 200 / 29,445 B UNCHALLENGED in the same minute. Treat a /cgi/ls 403 as UNANSWERED-with-a-known-200-history and re-run in a later window; never as an empty catalogue.
hathitrust.full_view_text_is_a_different_question: rightsCode pd / usRightsString 'Full view' from the catalog API says the item CAN be opened by a human, not that a script can open it: /cgi/pt?id=<hdl>&view=1up&seq=1 (the viewer for a Full-view item) answered 403 Cf-Mitigated: challenge at 13:47Z. So scripted HathiTrust currently delivers RECORDS + RIGHTS, and the page text still needs a browser or the Internet Archive copy of the same item.
hathitrust.fake_negative_warning: facet=DateRange:"1960-1969" (a plausible but NONEXISTENT field) is silently accepted, echoed as an active filter, and returns 'No results match your search' for a control query that really has 2,284 hits. ht_search_url now refuses any facet field outside bothPublishDateRange/pubDateRange.

google_books.working_shape: https://books.google.com/books/feeds/volumes?q=<quoted phrase>&maxResults=10  — legacy Data API, Atom, no key, no GCP quota. Real volumeIds, dc:title/date/creator/publisher, gbs:viewability (all_pages/partial/no_pages) and the matched page as pg=PA138.
google_books.what_was_wrong: Not the request shape: the code already used www.googleapis.com/books/v1/volumes. The 429 body says why — reason=rateLimitExceeded, quota_limit 'Queries per day', consumer = Google's SHARED ANONYMOUS project project_number:624717413613, quota_limit_value '0'. Keyless v1 is switched OFF for everyone: no delay, no backoff and no second egress changes it. It needs a key (--gb-key / GOOGLE_BOOKS_API_KEY).
google_books.real_limit_documented_not_pretended_away: Keyless gives SNIPPET-level text, NOT full text. CORRECTED 2026-09-25 (second pass over the saved bodies): there is no <gbs:snippet>/<gbs:searchResult> node, which an earlier note here misread as 'no snippet at all' — but 44 of the 50 entries in the five verified 200 feeds carry a <dc:description> of 178-283 characters, i.e. Google's matched-page snippet, plus gbs:viewability and a pg= page pointer. So the feed can put a sentence of the periodical page in front of a researcher; it cannot put the page there. The books.google.com BROWSING html for a matched page answers 403 'your computer or network may be sending automated queries'. openSearch:totalResults read 300 for three unrelated queries: a display cap, never a count.
google_books.verified_counts: 2026-09-25, HTTP 200 each: '"wal-mart" "five-and-dime"' -> 10 volumes; '"Wal-Mart" Bentonville Rogers' -> 10 volumes incl. 'The World of Wal-Mart' 2013 pg=PA138 partial; '"Apple Computer" Cupertino shareholder' -> 10 volumes incl. InfoWorld 1983-02-28 with viewability=all_pages and a matched page (a real periodical hit). RE-VERIFIED LIVE 13:48Z the same three queries plus '"Charter Med" Minneapolis' -> 200 / 25,023 / 23,608 / 23,665 B, byte-identical to the cached bodies, while the v1 control re-answered 429 with quota_limit_value 0.

_endpoint_verification_20260925.internet_archive_and_corporate_print: Unchanged and still the two working text-bearing routes (200s on 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-25); the FY1972-FY1997 Wal-Mart annual-report run and Apple's 1989 creator-scoped corporate print are the verified exemplars.

per_source_caps._note: Caps must cover EVERY configured task: a cap below the task count writes 'SKIPPED: per-source cap reached' UNANSWERED rows for tasks that were never even attempted, which is the unqueried-family-as-null error in a new costume. 2026-09-25: chronicling_america 17 (was 14 against 17 tasks), hathitrust 9 (was 8 against 9). Being polite is the per-host delay and the 5-consecutive-failure hard stop, not a number here: the 17 CA tasks cost at most 5 fresh requests before the hard stop halts the host, and cached URLs cost 0.

tasks._note: DIRECTORY/CATALOGUE canary, not evidence of any story. If this returns 200 the CA zone stopped challenging scripted clients and the page searches below become live; if it returns 403 with Cf-Mitigated: challenge the family stays UNANSWERED for the whole corpus. Cheap way to keep the question open instead of re-guessing it.

CORRECTED. Brand with the hyphen the full-text index has to match, the company's own town, and the window that opens with the name (1960) and the first store (1962). The old set never once searched 'Wal-Mart'.
Rogers is where the first Wal-Mart Discount City opened (1962) per the registrant's own FY1980 statement (W-63). The old set had no Rogers query at all.

Place-name correction as briefed: the registrant's own FY1980 origin statement (W-63, sources/WALMART_AR_1980.txt) says the 1945 Ben Franklin franchise was at Newport, ARKANSAS, and the FY1973 store-location list prints Newport among the Arkansas stores (W-43).

DO NOT DELETE. The brief's correction ('Newport is in Arkansas, not Missouri') and the standard Walton biography (1945 Ben Franklin franchise, Newport, Missouri) disagree, and the company's own 1980 statement is what W-63 cites. Both states are in scope anyway: FY1980 says the Walton brothers' fifteen variety stores were 'most of them in small towns in Arkansas, Missouri and Kansas'. Querying only one town would manufacture a fake negative for the other, which is the exact error this file was rewritten to remove.
The franchise signage is what a 1950s small-town paper would have printed; 'waltons' as a bare token (the old query) is neither the store name nor a searchable phrase.
Hyphen form replaced by the unhyphenated form: NDNP OCR tokenises hyphens inconsistently, so '"five-and-dime"' (the old query) is a coin-flip. Keep both until a live CA response can compare them.

params.q: "Walton's" store AND mediatype:texts AND YEAR:[1945 TO 1965]
walton (retailing OR "variety store" OR "five and dime") AND mediatype:texts AND YEAR:[1945 TO 1965]

tasks._note: CORRECTED brand + town, verified live 2026-09-25 on the semicolon grammar. Full View means the item text can be opened; that is what makes this family carry contemporaneous text for pre-1994 companies.

tasks._note: PLUMBING CONTROL, not company evidence. It MUST return >0. If this row ever comes back 0 while the host answers 200, the endpoint or the facet grammar broke — that is a defect in our request, not an absence in the record, and every null in this file must be re-read.

tasks.query_label: HT CATALOG brief record for htid pur1.32754078649484 (verified 200 JSON, unchallenged)
tasks._note: THE SCRIPTED-CLIENT HATHITRUST ROUTE. Verified 2026-09-25 from this machine's own Python client: /api/volumes/brief/htid/<hdl>.json answers HTTP 200 with records{titles,publishDates,isbns,oclcs,lccns} + items[]{htid,itemURL,rightsCode,usRightsString,orig} — no Cloudflare challenge — while /cgi/ls from the same client 403s Cf-Mitigated: challenge and the browsable /Record/003910927 page 403s too. So: rights/metadata for a known item is open to a script; searching the full-text index is not. The htid here is copied verbatim from the data-hdl of the live /cgi/ls response above ('Ice in the Ozarks', Arkansas, 2004, rightsCode 'pd' = public domain, usRightsString 'Full view'), which makes it the cheapest proof that a pre-1994-relevant Full-view item exists; the text itself still has to be fetched from the itemURL.
Feeds endpoint (keyless). Metadata + matched page, no snippet text — see _endpoint_verification_20260925.

tasks._note: One request, kept on purpose: it re-proves the diagnosis instead of letting it become folklore. If it ever returns 200 the keyless JSON API is back and the endpoint default can move to v1.

REFERENCE EXEMPLAR OF A HIT. Verified live 2026-09-24: this exact param set returns numFound=27, the printed Wal-Mart Stores FY1972-FY1997 annual-report run that flipped the Walmart depth verdict from forensic-core to exemplar (company_002_walmart/research/B_periodical_retest.md). The original probe had asserted 'pre-IPO financials are UNDOCUMENTED at Tier 1' while never querying digitised books or bound corporate print.
Tests the documented gap: FY1970/FY1971 reports are absent from IA (retest WR-16). A numFound=0 here is a null on THESE PARAMS, not on the family.

tasks.query_label: CA Richard Burke Minnesota 1974-1988 (REPLACES the phantom term 'Burdic')
tasks._note: THE FAKE NEGATIVE THIS REWRITE EXISTS FOR. The shipped set searched "Burdic" — not the founder, not a Minnesota town, not a word in any source: founder and chairman until 1988-02 is RICHARD T. BURKE (UH-12/UH-13/UH-30, DEF 14A director tables). 'Burdic' 0-hits (also 0 in the Minnesota Medicine index grep) were read as silence about the founder. Burke is a common surname, so the person query must carry the place and the industry terms; a bare '"Burke"' hit is a lead, never the founder, until the text is read.

_corporate_print_reference_exemplar._what_it_proves: Family 5 is the family that REVERSED a depth verdict. The complete printed Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. annual-report run FY1972-FY1997 sits on Internet Archive with text layers, free; the probe that rated Walmart 'forensic-core' had asserted 'pre-IPO financials are UNDOCUMENTED at Tier 1' and 'annual-report text = paper, not EDGAR' without ever querying digitised books or bound corporate print. See founders_playbook/01_companies/company_002_walmart/research/B_periodical_retest.md.

reference_hit.verified_query: (title:(walmart) OR title:("wal-mart stores")) AND (title:(annual) OR title:(reports) OR title:(yearbook)) AND mediatype:(texts) AND YEAR:[1970 TO 1998]

example_item.title: 1972 Annual Report For Walmart Stores Inc

_corporate_print_reference_exemplar.field_verification: title:/creator:/mediatype:/YEAR:[a TO b] clauses and fl[] return fields confirmed by live advancedsearch calls; server/dir/files[].name/metadata.{title,date,year} confirmed by a live archive.org/metadata/<id> call. NOTHING in this family uses an unverified parameter.
known_query_traps: title:("wal-mart") does NOT match an item titled 'Walmart Stores' — hyphen/quote tokenisation is unreliable, so always OR the hyphenless form.

Unscoped conjunctions (walmart AND "annual report" AND YEAR:[..]) return token noise (CIA reading-room documents, Compute! magazine). numFound>0 from such a query is NOT evidence — that is WR-17 of the Walmart retest.
archive.org/download/<id>/<file> 302s to a CDN whose TLS certificate is expired from this network; use the server+dir route recorded above.

A 404/0-hit from ANY family is a statement about the parameter set that produced it. The three additions of 2026-09-25 to that list: a HathiTrust date facet with the wrong FIELD name returns 'No results match your search' for a query that has 2,284 hits; a UnitedHealth person query on a surname nobody in the record ('Burdic') returns 0 for a company whose founder is Burke; an Apple periodical query set that does not exist at all returns nothing for a family never searched.
